children: SYDNEY--The Australian government 10-year bond yield dipped below 5.0% Friday, in line with a selloff in Treasurys as financial markets moved to assess the likelihood that a Democrat-led Congress will hamper the race to develop artificial intelligence.

The yield on the 10-year government bond yield fell below 5.00% for the first time since late August in early Asia trading, extending a retreat that has been in play over the last month. It traded at 5.01% as of 0205 GMT, slightly higher from an earlier low of 4.99%, a level not seen since late August.
The 10-year yield soared at a 15-year high just above 5.40% in early October amid forecasts it would go even higher.
"The bottom in yields is hard to call here from here," said Jack Chambers, interest rate strategist at ANZ.
"The U.S. growth story is still strong right now, and at some point investors should expect that to offset concerns about the possibility of future AI regulation," he adds.
At the very least, those themes will be the key market tension for a while yet, he said.
Market price action reflects a classic flight-to-safety move, said Masahiko Loo, chief fixed income strategist at State Street Investment Management.

While the blue wave in the U.S. raises the prospect of greater scrutiny around data centers and AI infrastructure, it does not signal the end of the AI investment cycle, he said. "Corporate investment, strategic competition and demand for compute remain intact."
Loo expects market volatility to settle as markets refocus on longer-term fundamentals, with looming release of U.S. non-farm payrolls likely the nearest catalyst.
"History also argues against over reacting to election headlines, with the S&P 500 having not declined in the 12 months following a U.S. midterm election since 1930," he added.
The bond market appears to be returning to it normal function with income re-emerging as the primary driver of returns, while diversification benefits are being restored, Loo said.
